channel.title: The Model Note
channel.description: Practical notes for choosing and deploying AI models and agents — transparent decision guides, workflow tools, and implementation write-ups.

item.title: Stop asking agents for permission at every step. Start deciding where approval belongs.
item.description: Three approval models—per action, per plan, and per boundary—and a practical default for a small team running its first supervised agent pilot.

item.title: Before you add another agent, build a five-case evaluation suite.
item.description: A compact way to move beyond glossy demos: real tasks, observable outcomes, trace review, a failure case, and repeatability.

item.title: The most useful first agent may be a workflow that does not look autonomous.
item.description: A decision guide for choosing the least-complex AI system that can improve a recurring task—and knowing when an agent is actually justified.

item.title: Before you trust an agent, make its work easy to replay.
item.description: A practical review packet helps a team inspect the request, boundary, path, outcome, and human decision—without mistaking a polished summary for evidence.

item.title: Context is a budget. Spend it on the next decision.
item.description: A practical way to give an agent the smallest trustworthy packet for the job, then leave a handoff a human or fresh session can actually use.

item.title: We spent $0.05 testing Jev. Its calibration held. The pipeline around it didn’t.
item.description: A pre-registered 1,000-call check of TypeSafe’s System One model: stated confidence tracked accuracy in every bin we could test, and it answered all 1,150 calls with typed output — while a chat baseline failed to return usable JSON on a third of calls.
